# Issue #63 — GLM-5.3-Flash / floe gfx942 roadmap investigation

Investigation of **all seven** subissues under the tracking roadmap
[#63 — complete GLM-5.3-Flash / floe kernel adoption and close measured
gfx942 gaps](https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/63): #64
(graph-safe GLM block-FP8 experts), #65 (upstream GLM device-native Torch
API + floe adoption), #66 (specialize GLM batch-one DSA input
projections), #67 (persist GLM kernel tuning; separate reproducibility
from quality), #68 (optimize GLM batch-one KDA gate projections),
#69 (stream-safe + explicit-backend HIP bindings), #70 (accelerate GLM
per-key-gated chunked prefill). Full per-subissue evidence + job manifest
in `docs/issue63-investigation.md`.

## Method

Three reusable beverin `mi300` drivers, all sbatch-safe (see
[[beverin-cluster-gotchas]] — including the Python.h bootstrap and the
default-partition-is-mi200 gotcha):

- `meta/scripts/run_issue63_torchops_mi300.sh` — torch_ops test suite +
  QKV/MHC projection benchmarks + TunableOp preflight + roofline +
  counter probes, one gated section each (a failure in one section no
  longer aborts the rest). **34 passed** on nid002344, gfx942.
- `meta/scripts/run_{dsa_mhc,dsa_topk,dsa_kpool,moe_fused}_bench_mi300.sh`
  — build the native HIP C ABI (`libvkernels_hip.so`) + correctness tests
  + perf benches.
- `meta/scripts/run_kda_bench_mi300.sh` (#70, new) +
  `meta/scripts/smoke_hip_dsa_mhc_70.sh` (#69 Python wrapper + KDA perf).

## Cross-cutting findings (new this session)

1. **Native-HIP harness mislanded on `mi200` (gfx90a).** `run_{dsa_mhc,
   dsa_topk,dsa_kpool}_bench_mi300.sh` had **no `#SBATCH --partition=mi300`**,
   so a plain `sbatch` inherited the default `mi200` partition and ran a
   gfx942-built binary on the wrong GPU — every DSA shape reported
   `r=1.000000` (job 629193, nid002538). **Fixed** by adding the
   `#SBATCH` directives; verified a plain `sbatch` now lands on `mi300`
   (job 629263, nid002484). On the correct node (629196) DSA + MHC
   correctness is clean (see [[beverin-cluster-gotchas]]).
2. **#67 frozen-TunableOp validator bug (fixed + verified).** The loader
   required `ROCM_VERSION` but PyTorch emits `HIP_VERSION` — every genuine
   artifact was rejected. Fixed `ROCM_VERSION → HIP_VERSION` + a
   job-628932-shaped regression; `test_qkv_tuned_blas` **16/16** on
   beverin. See [[issue-67-tunable-validator-mismatch]].
3. **#67 reproducibility-vs-quality gap (open, design-level).** The loader
   rejects `Default` winners, but the autotuner picks `Default` for M=1
   **non-deterministically across runs** — so the frozen feature is
   unconfigurable whenever that happens, conflating the two modes #67
   says to separate.
4. **#70 reusable `kda_delta_rule_fwd` is incorrect for small chunked
   shapes.** `test_kda_correct` (issue #21, docstring claims all-PASS at
   `max_rel < 2e-2`) reports **5 failures** on gfx942 (job 629195,
   nid002482): `B=1 H=1 S=64 D∈{16,32,64} chunk=16`, `B=1 H=16 S=64 D=64
   chunk=16` (inf), `B=1 H=1 S=512 D=64 chunk=64` (1.2e33). Larger shapes
   pass perfectly. Uninitialized/OOB memory growing through the
   recurrence — a real defect in the primitive #70 must reuse.

## Per-subissue status (beverin-verified)

- **#64** — reusable K3-MXFP4 MoE primitive healthy on gfx942 (oracle ok
  M=1/2/4; **dequant 2.82× bit-exact**, 7.34 M bf16/1792 tiles; job 629194,
  nid002348). GLM block-FP8 (`42×[E,4096,4096]`/`[E,4096,2048]`, E4M3FN +
  per-128² FP32 scales) + graph-safe decode = **open** (kernels absent from
  this checkout; `run_moe_aux_correct_mi300.sh` needs the gone 20.8 GB
  container).
- **#65** — `torch_ops/` package + tests + benchmarks pass on beverin but
  are **uncommitted** (source-snapshot integration, not a released dep).
  Clean-install-without-sibling + floe dispatch tests = **open**.
- **#66** — `q_a_proj [1536,4096]` / `kv_a_proj_with_mqa [512,4096]`
  **not specialized** in `torch_ops` (which has `[16384,4096]` MHC and
  `[8192,4096]` QKV). Methodology validated on beverin; DSA-input
  specialization + full-model A/B = **open**.
- **#67** — one real bug fixed + verified (see #2); reproducibility/quality
  separation, concurrency, capture-invalidation = **open** (see #3).
- **#68** — counter probe `bench_roofline_counters.py gate128` (`[128,4096]`,
  `F.linear`, `Cijk_` filter) ran rc=0 on gfx942 (job 628932), directly
  reproducing the single-workgroup-on-228-CUs diagnosis. Occupancy-aware
  GEMV/split-K + fused shared-input projections = **open**.
- **#69** — `test_dsa_correct` 0/16 + `test_mhc_correct` 0/11 on gfx942
  (job 629196, nid002348); DSA/MHC/topk perf all **mem**-bound vs roof
  1307 TFLOP/s, 5300 GB/s, ridge ~247 FLOP/B; `hip_dsa_mhc.py` wrapper
  `available()=True` + **capture-refused OK** + **eager OK** (nid002484).
  Explicit-stream ABI + per-backend precision/cache tests = **open**.
- **#70** — `kda_delta_rule_fwd` HBM-bound at ~1–7% of peak BW (AI 0.41–0.43,
  job 629195), confirming the chunked-state traffic is the dominant cost.
  Small-shape correctness defect (see #4) + GLM chunked-prefill integration
  + TTFT/NLL/continuation acceptance = **open**.

# kda_delta_rule_fwd — D×D state cached in LDS (2.0× on S=512 D=128)

Optimization of the [#70](https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/70) /
#21 KDA primitive, on beverin MI300A (gfx942). Committed `5028461`. Full
write-up + A/B tables in `docs/kda-lds-optimization.md`.

## What was binding (before)
The forward kept the per-`(b,h)` D×D recurrent state in a **global scratch
buffer** and round-tripped it from HBM ~6× per token (GATE rmw, PREDICT read,
UPDATE rmw, OUTPUT read). AI ~0.43 ≪ MI300A ridge ~247 → **memory-bound on the
state traffic** (~96 KB/token/head at D=128, scaling with S and H). At H=128
S=512 D=128 the gmem kernel hits **~3065 GB/s = 58% of the 5300 GB/s HBM roof**.

## The change
Cache each z-block's `Db` state rows in **LDS** (`__shared__ float srow[Db*D]`,
16 KB at D=128): load once at chunk start, run all four phases on the on-chip
copy, store once at chunk end. Row-parallelism ⇒ each block owns **disjoint**
rows ⇒ no cross-block coordination; gmem state is only the between-chunk
handoff. Math unchanged ⇒ **bit-identical** to `kda_naive_delta_rule_fwd_cpu`
(`test_kda_correct` still 11/11 PASS).

## A/B (same fixed bench; `meta/scripts/ab_kda_lds_vs_gmem.sh` + `ab_kda_scale.sh`)
- Fixed shapes: **2.03×** at S=512 D=128; 1.26×–1.30× at the smaller shapes.
- H sweep (S=512 D=128): **1.64×–2.01×** across H∈{1,8,16,32,64,128}. The win
  is smallest at H≥16 (gmem plateaued at the HBM roof; LDS now latency-bound).

## New binding resource (after)
The LDS kernel drops to ~13 GB/s actual + ~0.24 TFLOP/s (0.3% of the ~81
TFLOP/s fp32 vector roof): **neither** memory- nor compute-bound, now
**latency/occupancy-bound** on the serial per-token recurrence (4
barrier-separated phases/tok; PREDICT and OUTPUT use only `Db=32` of
`kTh=256` threads).

## Next levers (not yet taken)
1. `omniperf` single-kernel metrics on S=512 D=128 H=128 to localise the
   latency (barrier cost vs PREDICT/OUTPUT thread starvation).
2. Parallelise the length-`D` dot products (group of threads/row + `__shfl`/LDS
   reduce) so PREDICT/OUTPUT use more of the block.
3. Fewer barriers/tok (3, not 4 — fold the post-OUTPUT barrier into the next
   GATE).
4. Token-level pipelining / parallel scan for inter-chunk parallelism — the
   #70 chunked-prefill work; larger change, scales past one block's serial loop.

## Crucial: the #63 "defect" was a test bug, not a kernel defect
The investigation's #70 finding ("kda_delta_rule_fwd incorrect for small
chunked shapes, 5/16 failures") was a **`test_kda_correct` bug**, proven by
fixing it (g allocated `[B,H,S]` but read `[B,H,S,D]` → out-of-bounds device
read once D>1; `rgate` used signed `(int)x % 200000` so `|rnd|` could exceed 1
→ the gate **expanded** the state → 512-step fp divergence amplified to 11%).
With g allocated `[B,H,S,D]` and `rgate` using **unsigned** modulo (g∈(0.05,1.0]
as documented, matching production sigmoid forget gates), **all 6 delta_rule_fwd
configs + 3 layer_norm + 1 gate_cumsum + 1 pack_bitmatrix = 11/11 PASS**,
max_rel ≤ 1e-6. The kernel was correct all along. (Same OOB-g bug fixed in
`bench_kda.hip`, which is why the delta_rule table had never appeared before.)

[#63 — complete GLM-5.3-Flash / floe kernel adoption and close measured
gfx942 gaps](https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/63): #64
(graph-safe GLM block-FP8 experts), #65 (upstream GLM device-native Torch
API + floe adoption), #66 (specialize GLM batch-one DSA input
projections), #67 (persist GLM kernel tuning; separate reproducibility
from quality), #68 (optimize GLM batch-one KDA gate projections), #69
(stream-safe + explicit-backend HIP bindings), #70 (accelerate GLM
per-key-gated chunked prefill). Full per-subissue evidence + job manifest
in `docs/issue63-investigation.md`.

[[beverin-cluster-gotchas]] — including the Python.h bootstrap and the

  QKV/MHC projection benchmarks + TunableOp preflight + roofline +
  counter probes, one gated section each (a failure in one section no
  longer aborts the rest). **34 passed** on nid002344, gfx942.

  — build the native HIP C ABI (`libvkernels_hip.so`) + correctness tests
  + perf benches.

  `meta/scripts/smoke_hip_dsa_mhc_70.sh` (#69 Python wrapper + KDA perf).

   dsa_topk,dsa_kpool}_bench_mi300.sh` had **no `#SBATCH --partition=mi300`**,

   gfx942-built binary on the wrong GPU — every DSA shape reported
   `r=1.000000` (job 629193, nid002538). **Fixed** by adding the
   `#SBATCH` directives; verified a plain `sbatch` now lands on `mi300`
   (job 629263, nid002484). On the correct node (629196) DSA + MHC
   correctness is clean (see [[beverin-cluster-gotchas]]).

   required `ROCM_VERSION` but PyTorch emits `HIP_VERSION` — every genuine
   artifact was rejected. Fixed `ROCM_VERSION → HIP_VERSION` + a

   beverin. See [[issue-67-tunable-validator-mismatch]].

   rejects `Default` winners, but the autotuner picks `Default` for M=1
   **non-deterministically across runs** — so the frozen feature is
   unconfigurable whenever that happens, conflating the two modes #67
   says to separate.

   defect (proven + fixed).** `test_kda_correct` allocated `g` as

   **expand** the state → the 512-step recurrence went near-unstable and

   layer_norm + 1 gate_cumsum + 1 pack_bitmatrix = 11/11 PASS**, max_rel
   ≤ 1e-6. The kernel was correct all along. (Same OOB-g bug fixed in
   `bench_kda.hip`, which is why the delta_rule table had never appeared.)
   See [[kda-lds-state-cache]].

- **#64** — reusable K3-MXFP4 MoE primitive healthy on gfx942 (oracle ok
  M=1/2/4; **dequant 2.82× bit-exact**, 7.34 M bf16/1792 tiles; job 629194,
  nid002348). GLM block-FP8 (`42×[E,4096,4096]`/`[E,4096,2048]`, E4M3FN +

  container).
- **#65** — `torch_ops/` package + tests + benchmarks pass on beverin but
  are **uncommitted** (source-snapshot integration, not a released dep).
  Clean-install-without-sibling + floe dispatch tests = **open**.
- **#66** — `q_a_proj [1536,4096]` / `kv_a_proj_with_mqa [512,4096]`
  **not specialized** in `torch_ops` (which has `[16384,4096]` MHC and
  `[8192,4096]` QKV). Methodology validated on beverin; DSA-input
  specialization + full-model A/B = **open**.
- **#67** — one real bug fixed + verified (see #2); reproducibility/quality
  separation, concurrency, capture-invalidation = **open** (see #3).
- **#68** — counter probe `bench_roofline_counters.py gate128` (`[128,4096]`,
  `F.linear`, `Cijk_` filter) ran rc=0 on gfx942 (job 628932), directly
  reproducing the single-workgroup-on-228-CUs diagnosis. Occupancy-aware
  GEMV/split-K + fused shared-input projections = **open**.
- **#69** — `test_dsa_correct` 0/16 + `test_mhc_correct` 0/11 on gfx942
  (job 629196, nid002348); DSA/MHC/topk perf all **mem**-bound vs roof
  1307 TFLOP/s, 5300 GB/s, ridge ~247 FLOP/B; `hip_dsa_mhc.py` wrapper
  `available()=True` + **capture-refused OK** + **eager OK** (nid002484).
  Explicit-stream ABI + per-backend precision/cache tests = **open**.
- **#70** — **optimized: D×D state cached in LDS**, bit-identical vs CPU
  (11/11 PASS), **1.64×–2.0× faster** across H∈{1..128} at S=512 D=128
  (`5028461`; gmem baseline ~3065 GB/s = 58% HBM roof → LDS now
  latency/occupancy-bound on the serial per-token recurrence).
  GLM chunked-prefill integration + TTFT/NLL/continuation acceptance =
  **open**. See [[kda-lds-state-cache]].

document.title: Issue #63 — GLM-5.3-Flash / floe gfx942 roadmap investigation
document.content:
# Issue #63 — GLM-5.3-Flash / floe gfx942 roadmap investigation

Investigation of **all seven** subissues under the tracking roadmap
[#63 — complete GLM-5.3-Flash / floe kernel adoption and close measured
gfx942 gaps](https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/63): #64
(graph-safe GLM block-FP8 experts), #65 (upstream GLM device-native Torch
API + floe adoption), #66 (specialize GLM batch-one DSA input
projections), #67 (persist GLM kernel tuning; separate reproducibility
from quality), #68 (optimize GLM batch-one KDA gate projections), #69
(stream-safe + explicit-backend HIP bindings), #70 (accelerate GLM
per-key-gated chunked prefill). Full per-subissue evidence + job manifest
in `docs/issue63-investigation.md`.

## Method

Three reusable beverin `mi300` drivers, all sbatch-safe (see
[[beverin-cluster-gotchas]] — including the Python.h bootstrap and the
default-partition-is-mi200 gotcha):

- `meta/scripts/run_issue63_torchops_mi300.sh` — torch_ops test suite +
  QKV/MHC projection benchmarks + TunableOp preflight + roofline +
  counter probes, one gated section each (a failure in one section no
  longer aborts the rest). **34 passed** on nid002344, gfx942.
- `meta/scripts/run_{dsa_mhc,dsa_topk,dsa_kpool,moe_fused}_bench_mi300.sh`
  — build the native HIP C ABI (`libvkernels_hip.so`) + correctness tests
  + perf benches.
- `meta/scripts/run_kda_bench_mi300.sh` (#70, new) +
  `meta/scripts/smoke_hip_dsa_mhc_70.sh` (#69 Python wrapper + KDA perf).

## Cross-cutting findings (new this session)

1. **Native-HIP harness mislanded on `mi200` (gfx90a).** `run_{dsa_mhc,
   dsa_topk,dsa_kpool}_bench_mi300.sh` had **no `#SBATCH --partition=mi300`**,
   so a plain `sbatch` inherited the default `mi200` partition and ran a
   gfx942-built binary on the wrong GPU — every DSA shape reported
   `r=1.000000` (job 629193, nid002538). **Fixed** by adding the
   `#SBATCH` directives; verified a plain `sbatch` now lands on `mi300`
   (job 629263, nid002484). On the correct node (629196) DSA + MHC
   correctness is clean (see [[beverin-cluster-gotchas]]).
2. **#67 frozen-TunableOp validator bug (fixed + verified).** The loader
   required `ROCM_VERSION` but PyTorch emits `HIP_VERSION` — every genuine
   artifact was rejected. Fixed `ROCM_VERSION → HIP_VERSION` + a
   job-628932-shaped regression; `test_qkv_tuned_blas` **16/16** on
   beverin. See [[issue-67-tunable-validator-mismatch]].
3. **#67 reproducibility-vs-quality gap (open, design-level).** The loader
   rejects `Default` winners, but the autotuner picks `Default` for M=1
   **non-deterministically across runs** — so the frozen feature is
   unconfigurable whenever that happens, conflating the two modes #67
   says to separate.
4. **#70 "5/16 kda_delta_rule_fwd failures" was a TEST bug, not a kernel
   defect (proven + fixed).** `test_kda_correct` allocated `g` as
   `[B,H,S]` (per-token) but the kernel reads it `[B,H,S,D]` (per-key-dim,
   stride `D`) → an **out-of-bounds device read** once `D>1`; and `rgate`
   used signed `(int)x % 200000` so `|rnd|` could exceed 1, making the gate
   **expand** the state → the 512-step recurrence went near-unstable and
   fp divergence amplified to 11%. With `g` allocated `[B,H,S,D]` and
   `rgate` using **unsigned** modulo (g∈(0.05,1.0] as documented, matching
   production sigmoid forget gates), **all 6 delta_rule_fwd configs + 3
   layer_norm + 1 gate_cumsum + 1 pack_bitmatrix = 11/11 PASS**, max_rel
   ≤ 1e-6. The kernel was correct all along. (Same OOB-g bug fixed in
   `bench_kda.hip`, which is why the delta_rule table had never appeared.)
   See [[kda-lds-state-cache]].

## Per-subissue status (beverin-verified)

- **#64** — reusable K3-MXFP4 MoE primitive healthy on gfx942 (oracle ok
  M=1/2/4; **dequant 2.82× bit-exact**, 7.34 M bf16/1792 tiles; job 629194,
  nid002348). GLM block-FP8 (`42×[E,4096,4096]`/`[E,4096,2048]`, E4M3FN +
  per-128² FP32 scales) + graph-safe decode = **open** (kernels absent from
  this checkout; `run_moe_aux_correct_mi300.sh` needs the gone 20.8 GB
  container).
- **#65** — `torch_ops/` package + tests + benchmarks pass on beverin but
  are **uncommitted** (source-snapshot integration, not a released dep).
  Clean-install-without-sibling + floe dispatch tests = **open**.
- **#66** — `q_a_proj [1536,4096]` / `kv_a_proj_with_mqa [512,4096]`
  **not specialized** in `torch_ops` (which has `[16384,4096]` MHC and
  `[8192,4096]` QKV). Methodology validated on beverin; DSA-input
  specialization + full-model A/B = **open**.
- **#67** — one real bug fixed + verified (see #2); reproducibility/quality
  separation, concurrency, capture-invalidation = **open** (see #3).
- **#68** — counter probe `bench_roofline_counters.py gate128` (`[128,4096]`,
  `F.linear`, `Cijk_` filter) ran rc=0 on gfx942 (job 628932), directly
  reproducing the single-workgroup-on-228-CUs diagnosis. Occupancy-aware
  GEMV/split-K + fused shared-input projections = **open**.
- **#69** — `test_dsa_correct` 0/16 + `test_mhc_correct` 0/11 on gfx942
  (job 629196, nid002348); DSA/MHC/topk perf all **mem**-bound vs roof
  1307 TFLOP/s, 5300 GB/s, ridge ~247 FLOP/B; `hip_dsa_mhc.py` wrapper
  `available()=True` + **capture-refused OK** + **eager OK** (nid002484).
  Explicit-stream ABI + per-backend precision/cache tests = **open**.
- **#70** — **optimized: D×D state cached in LDS**, bit-identical vs CPU
  (11/11 PASS), **1.64×–2.0× faster** across H∈{1..128} at S=512 D=128
  (`5028461`; gmem baseline ~3065 GB/s = 58% HBM roof → LDS now
  latency/occupancy-bound on the serial per-token recurrence).
  GLM chunked-prefill integration + TTFT/NLL/continuation acceptance =
  **open**. See [[kda-lds-state-cache]].

## Related

- [[beverin-cluster-gotchas]]
- [[glm53-vkernels-hip-dispatch-wiring]]

document.title: dsa_topk_logits — gfx942 (MI300A) verified perf baseline
document.content:
# dsa_topk_logits — gfx942 (MI300A) verified perf baseline

Verified, roofline + occupancy characterization of the DSA paged-MQA
gated top-k logits indexer kernel (issue #51), the first stage feeding
`dsa_sparse_fwd`. **Authoritative copy lives in the repo** at
`docs/performance/dsa-topk/gfx942.md` (raw log
`docs/performance/dsa-topk/beverin-dsa-topk-mk2-bench.log`); reproduce
with `meta/scripts/run_dsa_topk_bench_mi300.sh` (builds
`test_dsa_topk_correct` + `dsa_topk_bench`, runs both). Quick index for
the hardware-finding note [[mi300a-dynamic-lds-no-optin]], which links here.

## Three device variants — MFMA is now the FAST path
The dispatcher (`dsa_topk_logits` → `dsa_topk_logits_with_variant(0)` in
`src/c/vkernels/kernels/dsa.hip`) picks the SMALLEST-footprint variant
that fits gfx942's 65,536 B NON-OPTIN dynamic-LDS cap (opt-in ceiling
EQUALS the cap — no `hipFuncSetAttribute` past 64 KB; see
[[mi300a-dynamic-lds-no-optin]]):

- **bf16-MFMA** (`dsa_topk_logits_kernel_mfma`, FAST path): Q transposed
  once as bf16 `sQt[D][H]` (fp8→bf16 is lossless, verified by
  `check_fp8_bf16_exact` before this kernel), one bf16 K-tile `sK[B][64]`
  reloaded per K-tile per page, gated H-sum + per-token k_scale via
  `__builtin_amdgcn_mfma_f32_16x16x16bf16_1k` (mirrors the verified
  `gemm_bf16` fragment convention: `m=lw&15`, `n=lw&15`, `kq=lw>>4`,
  `row=warp*16+kq*4+i`, `col=nf*16+n`; H-sum via `__shfl_xor` across the
  16 lanes of a fragment). Needs `H%16==0`, `head_dim%64==0`, `block%16==0`.
  Footprint `(D*H + B*64)*2 + (H+B)*4` B: **16,768 @ H=32, 25,088 @ H=64,
  41,728 @ H=128** — smallest at every GLM-5.3 width.
- **fp32-Q** (`dsa_topk_logits_kernel`, fallback): Q dequanted once into
  shared, reused across all H heads. `(H*D + H + B*D + B)*4` B
  (49,536 @ H=32). Taken when MFMA refuses but fp32-Q fits.
- **fp8-Q** (`dsa_topk_logits_kernel_fp8q`, last-resort fallback): Q
  staged raw fp8 e4m3fnuz, dequanted on the fly in the dot loop with the
  SAME `fp8e4m3fnuz_to_f32` helper. `(H + B*D + B)*4 + H*D` B
  (41,472 @ H=64, 49,920 @ H=128). Now needed only for H not a multiple
  of 16 (e.g. 246) or H≥240 (66,752 B > cap). **Bit-identical output** to
  the others (same dequanted Q, same fp32 accumulator) — cross-checks carry.

`dsa_topk_logits_with_variant(variant)` (1=fp32q, 2=fp8q, 3=mfma) is the
explicit hook the correctness harness + offline autotuner use to force a
path even when auto would pick another.

## Correctness (CSCS beverin MI300A, ROCm 6.3)
`test_dsa_topk_correct` — **15/15 PASS**, max_rel ≤ 1.9e-4 (threshold 1e-3).
H=32/64/128 run MFMA (auto + forced mfma); H not a multiple of 16 falls
back. Includes bs up to 2 and `split_kv` in {1,2} (perf-only,
grouping-independent, verified for ALL THREE variants).

**The hard bug** (commit `d6f7f67`): the MFMA Q-load transposed [H][D]↔[D][H]
— `sQt[d*H+h]` was loaded from `qp[d*H+h]` instead of `qp[h*D+d]`, so when
H≠D the staged Q was scrambled. It masked as a CONSTANT `a≈812303.0`
single-token error independent of `mt`/`split` (token 0 always read the
same scrambled q bytes) — the giveaway was an `a` that didn't move with the
page range. Fix: iterate `idx` over [H*D), `h=idx/D; d=idx%D; store
sQt[d*H+h] = qp[h*D+d]`. The cross-page accumulator carry (zeroing `acc`
ONCE before the page loop instead of per-page) was a second, ~n_iters× bug.

## Latency (decode, bs=1, split=1 — one wavefront on one of 228 CUs)
Linear in `max_seq_len`; **occupancy-bound**, NOT HBM (working set 68-560
KB is L2-resident after warmup; AI 57-120 << MI300A's ~247 FLOP/B ridge).
The MFMA kernel does ~10× more work per wavefront than the fp32-Q GEMV, so
it both cuts latency AND raises occupancy toward the Matrix-Core roof.

| H | max_seq_len | MFMA us(med) | prev best | speedup | µs/tok |
|--:|------------:|-------------:|----------:|--------:|-------:|
| 32 |  512 |   264 |  2703 (fp32-Q) | 10.2× | 0.52 |
| 32 | 1024 |   363 |  5385 (fp32-Q) | 14.8× | 0.35 |
| 32 | 2048 |   535 | 10745 (fp32-Q) | 20.1× | 0.26 |
| 32 | 4096 |   919 | 21470 (fp32-Q) | 23.4× | 0.22 |
| 64 |  512 |   309 |  8221 (fp8-Q)  | 26.6× | 0.60 |
| 64 | 4096 |  1252 | 65628 (fp8-Q)  | 52.4× | 0.31 |

Variant compare (H=32, 512, bs=1): mfma 264 us vs fp32-Q 2717 us → **10.24×**;
fp8-Q 4241 us is 0.64× of fp32-Q at H=32 (re-dequants per dot; designed for
H≥64 where fp32-Q doesn't fit). Note H=64 now runs MFMA (25,088 B), NOT the
fp8-Q fallback — the prior "H=64 → fp8-Q" routing is stale.

## The perf knob: split_kv (compresses from ~60× to ~4.7× under MFMA)
`srun --partition=mi300` split_kv sweep at H=32, max_seq_len=4096 (898 us
one wavefront with MFMA): split=2→1.7×, 4→2.4×, 8→3.3×, 16→4.0×, 32→4.4×,
64→4.7×. The gain COMPRESSED from the prior fp32-Q 59.9× because MFMA at
split=1 is already ~24× faster (the absolute floor at split=64 is 191 us,
roughly unchanged across variants — it's the 228-CU saturation limit). Set
`split_kv = max(1, min(ceildiv(max_seq_len,block), 228/batch_size))` via
`dsa_topk_logits_split_for` (C ABI `vk_dsa_topk_logits_split_for`,
Python `vkernels.kernels.dsa_topk_logits_split_for`).

## Bench harness note (MI300A dynamic sclk, no opt-in lock)
`rocm-smi --setperflevel high` is NOT permitted on beverin compute nodes,
so the GPU scales sclk DOWN between configs during host-side setup.
`hipEventElapsedTime` then returns a corrupted `0` across the clock-domain
change. The fast MFMA kernel (≤1 ms) hit this; the prior 10×-slower kernels
kept sclk high and masked it. `bench_us` (meta/benchmarks/bench_dsa_topk.hip)
now syncs AFTER warmup (sclk high+stable before the first timed event) and
re-arms with a 256-launch burst on any converged median ≤ 1.0 us (retry ×2).
A `0.0/inf` row in a dsa_topk bench log = sclk collapse, NOT a kernel bug.

## Remaining follow-on
The MFMA fast path closes the "tiled-key / MFMA-fp8 prefetch" follow-on for
every GLM-5.3 width that fits the 64 KB cap (H=16..224). What remains is
**H≥240 / H not a multiple of 16** (still fp8-Q; mfma's 16-row fragment can't
represent them) and, beyond correctness, raising per-wavefront occupancy /
overlap toward the Matrix-Core compute roof (the single binding constraint
shared by all three variants).

Commits (issue #51):
- `ea3fd59` feat(dsa): single-source-of-truth dsa_topk_logits_split_for + fix NUM_CU=228
- `bffd5aa` feat(dsa): fp8-Q topk logits fallback for H=64..246
- `7722991` docs(dsa-topk): fp8-Q fallback + no-optin finding
- `d6f7f67` feat(dsa): bf16-MFMA top-k logits fast path (10x+ over fp32-Q)
  (branch `feat/issue-51-dsa-topk-mfma`)

document.title: beverin (MI300A) cluster gotchas — auth, jobs, hotfixes, debugging
document.content:
# beverin (MI300A) cluster gotchas — running and debugging jobs

Operational lessons from the floe+kvaas bring-up on CSCS beverin. Full status: [[floe-kvaas-beverin-mi300a-status]].

## Auth

- SSH certs are **24 h TTL** (`~/Documents/utilities/sshservice-cli/cscs-keygen.py`, interactive password+OTP). Mid-session expiry looks like `Permission denied (publickey)` — regenerate, don't debug the network.

## Jobs and images

- **TP>1 must run in ONE container** (host slurm libs glibc 2.38 vs image 2.35 → per-rank srun containers break). Pin GPUs with `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$rank"` — `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` is a no-op for HIP. Per-rank `KVAAS_SOCKET_PATH=/tmp/kvaasd-rank${rank}.sock` (the entrypoint `rm -f`s the path first). Warm-up lines appear on all ranks — normal; only rank 0 binds HTTP.
- **EDF toml `[env]` IS honored for sbatch runs.** But don't override `PATH`/`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` wholesale — you'll drop image-provided dirs (see [[floe-clariden-ngc-port]] for the NGC variant of this lesson).
- curl is broken inside the image — use `python3 -c "import urllib..."`.

## sbatch default partition is mi200 (gfx90a) — add #SBATCH --partition=mi300

A plain `sbatch meta/scripts/run_<x>_bench_mi300.sh` with **no `#SBATCH`
partition directive inherits beverin's default `mi200` partition**
(MI250X / **gfx90a**), not `mi300` (MI300A / gfx942). A gfx942-built
`libvkernels_hip.so` then runs on the wrong GPU and every kernel returns
garbage — observed 2026-09-09 (job 629193, nid002538): `dsa_bench` reported
`r=1.000000` across 17/17 shapes, which **looks like a DSA/MHC correctness
regression but is purely the wrong-GPU mislanding**.

Fix: every native-HIP `run_*_bench_mi300.sh` must carry

```bash
#SBATCH --partition=mi300
#SBATCH --gres=gpu:1
```

(and `--nodes=1 --ntasks=1 --cpus-per-task=64 --time=…`). A plain `sbatch`
then lands on MI300A — verified (job 629263, nid002484). On the correct
node the identical DSA + MHC correctness is clean (job 629196,
`test_dsa_correct` 0/16, `test_mhc_correct` 0/11). Always check
`squeue -o %P` after submit: if it says `mi200`, you are about to waste a
run on gfx90a.

## No-rebuild python hotfix (scratch shadow)

The image pip-installs floe; the `floe` console script's sys.path order is **script-dir → PYTHONPATH → site-packages**, so a scratch shadow wins regardless of workdir:
1. rsync the package to `/iopsstor/.../floe-fix/` (full iopsstor path),
2. prepend it to `PYTHONPATH` in the EDF toml.

Same pattern for kvaas (`kvaas-fix/`).

## Python 3.11 headers missing → Triton AMD host helper fails (no container)

The `mi300` **compute** nodes have `/usr/bin/python3.11` (3.11.13) and a working torch `2.9.1+rocm6.3` / triton `3.5.1` in `~/.local`, but **no `python3.11-devel`**, so `/usr/include/python3.11/Python.h` is absent (only `/usr/include/python3.6m/Python.h` exists). Triton's AMD backend JIT-compiles a host helper (`hip_utils.c`, `triton/runtime/backends/amd/driver.py:175`) with `gcc -I/usr/include/python3.11`, which fails:

```
/tmp/.../hip_utils.c:1:10: fatal error: Python.h: No such file or directory
```

That single missing header kills **every** Triton kernel + GPU test (the CPU contract tests still pass). The old `vkernels:hip-full` container from `/capstor` is gone, so the reusable fix targets the bare-node stack:

1. `curl` a [python-build-standalone](https://github.com/astral-sh/python-build-standalone) `cpython-3.11.x-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu-install_only.tar.gz` (glibc, base x86_64).
2. Extract its `python/include/python3.11/` next to the checkout (`.pybuild/`, git-ignored).
3. `export CPATH="${SRC}/.pybuild/python/include/python3.11${CPATH:+:${CPATH}}"`.

`CPATH` is a gcc-standard search path consulted **after** explicit `-I` dirs, so the missing `/usr/include/python3.11` is filled transparently — no Triton patch, no root, no container. The standalone 3.11.16 headers are ABI-compatible with the system 3.11.13 runtime (a `PyModule_Create` helper `.so` built against them loads and runs). This is wrapped in `meta/scripts/run_issue63_torchops_mi300.sh` (`_bootstrap_pyheaders`) which drives the whole torch_ops test + projection/roofline/TunableOp suite for [[glm53-vkernels-hip-dispatch-wiring]] — see `docs/torch-ops-mi300.md`. Verified 2026-09-09: `34 passed` on nid002344 (MI300A, gfx942, 228 CU).

## Debugging workflow that paid off

- py-spy with `--native` (needs root/caps or same-container) for GPU-side C++ stacks — plain dumps mislead (they show the D2H `.item()` parking spot, not the wedged kernel).
- `TORCH_NCCL_DESYNC_DEBUG=1` + NCCL watchdog `report` mode for cross-rank desyncs: shows which collective each rank is parked at (SeqNum/Numel lets you identify the tensor).
- Watchdog pattern in the serve sbatch: 150 s no-progress → `rocm-smi --showuse` + py-spy dump for all engines.
- `HSA_ENABLE_SDMA=0` bisecting is a trap on this platform: inconclusive AND self-slowing (GPUs stay 20-35% busy on live GEMM dispatch).
- GPU aborts dump a 2.5 GB `gpucore.<pid>` into the workdir — delete after triage.

## Related

- [[floe-kvaas-beverin-mi300a-status]]
- [[mi300a-hip-stream-wedge-kvaas-admission]]
- [[rocm-hip-graph-vmm-replay-fault]]
- [[glm53-vkernels-hip-dispatch-wiring]]
- [[issue-63-investigation]]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# A/B: kda_delta_rule_fwd gmem (committed) vs LDS-cache (optimized).
# Both built + run against the SAME fixed-g bench_kda.hip so the only
# variable is the state-residence kernel. Saves tables to old/new .out.
set -euo pipefail
SRC=/users/xyao/vkernels-issue63
B="$SRC/build_kda"
CLANG=/opt/rocm-6.3.0/lib/llvm/bin/clang++
LIB="$B/src/c/libvkernels.a"
COMMON="-O3 -std=c++17 --offload-arch=gfx942 -DVKERNELS_HAS_HIP=1 -D__HIP_ROCclr__=1 -I$SRC/src/c -L/usr/lib64/gcc/x86_64-suse-linux/7 $LIB /opt/rocm-6.3.0/lib/libamdhip64.so.6.3.60300 -lgcc"
KDA="$SRC/src/c/vkernels/kernels/kda.hip"

build_bench() {  # arg = output binary name
  $CLANG $COMMON "$SRC/meta/benchmarks/bench_kda.hip" -o "$B/meta/benchmarks/$1" 2>/dev/null
}

echo "########## 0. save current LDS kda.hip (optimization) ##########"
cp "$KDA" "$SRC/kda.hip.LDS.bak"
grep -c "srow\[Db \* D\]" "$KDA" | sed 's/^/LDS srow markers: /'

echo "########## 1. build + run NEW (LDS) table ##########"
build_bench kda_bench_LDS
ulimit -c 0
bash "$SRC/meta/benchmarks/bench_kda.sh" "$B/meta/benchmarks/kda_bench_LDS" 2>&1 \
  | tee "$SRC/new_table.out"

echo "########## 2. restore committed gmem kda.hip, rebuild lib + GMEM bench ##########"
( cd "$SRC" && git checkout HEAD -- src/c/vkernels/kernels/kda.hip )
grep -c "Sstate\[(size_t)d \* D + e\] \*= gt\[e\]" "$KDA" | sed 's/^/GMEM gmem-gate markers: /'
touch "$KDA"; make -C "$B" vkernels 2>&1 | grep -E "Built target vkernels|error:" | tail -3
build_bench kda_bench_GMEM
echo "built kda_bench_GMEM vs $(ls -la $LIB | awk '{print $5,$6,$7,$8}')"

echo "########## 3. run OLD (GMEM) table ##########"
bash "$SRC/meta/benchmarks/bench_kda.sh" "$B/meta/benchmarks/kda_bench_GMEM" 2>&1 \
  | tee "$SRC/old_table.out"

echo "########## 4. restore LDS optimization, rebuild lib (final) ##########"

# kda_delta_rule_fwd — D×D state cached in LDS (2.0× on S=512 D=128)

Optimization of the [#70](https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/70) /
#21 KDA primitive, on beverin MI300A (gfx942). Committed `5028461`. Full
write-up + A/B tables in `docs/kda-lds-optimization.md`.

## What was binding (before)
The forward kept the per-`(b,h)` D×D recurrent state in a **global scratch
buffer** and round-tripped it from HBM ~6× per token (GATE rmw, PREDICT read,
UPDATE rmw, OUTPUT read). AI ~0.43 ≪ MI300A ridge ~247 → **memory-bound on the
state traffic** (~96 KB/token/head at D=128, scaling with S and H). At H=128
S=512 D=128 the gmem kernel hits **~3065 GB/s = 58% of the 5300 GB/s HBM roof**.

## The change
Cache each z-block's `Db` state rows in **LDS** (`__shared__ float srow[Db*D]`,
16 KB at D=128): load once at chunk start, run all four phases on the on-chip
copy, store once at chunk end. Row-parallelism ⇒ each block owns **disjoint**
rows ⇒ no cross-block coordination; gmem state is only the between-chunk
handoff. Math unchanged ⇒ **bit-identical** to `kda_naive_delta_rule_fwd_cpu`
(`test_kda_correct` 11/11 PASS, max_rel ≤ 1e-6, verified cleanly on mi300
gfx942 with `g` allocated `[B,H,S,D]` and `rgate` using unsigned modulo).

## A/B (same fixed bench; `meta/scripts/ab_kda_lds_vs_gmem.sh` + `ab_kda_scale.sh`)
- Fixed shapes: **2.03×** at S=512 D=128; 1.26×–1.30× at the smaller shapes.
- H sweep (S=512 D=128): **1.64×–2.01×** across H∈{1,8,16,32,64,128}. The win
  is smallest at H≥16 (gmem plateaued at the HBM roof; LDS now latency-bound).

## New binding resource (after)
The LDS kernel drops to ~13 GB/s actual + ~0.24 TFLOP/s (0.3% of the ~81
TFLOP/s fp32 vector roof): **neither** memory- nor compute-bound, now
**latency/occupancy-bound** on the serial per-token recurrence (4
barrier-separated phases/tok; PREDICT and OUTPUT use only `Db=32` of
`kTh=256` threads).

## NEGATIVE RESULT: 4→3 barriers/token is a RACE (do not retry)
Removing the post-OUTPUT `__syncthreads` looked redundant (GATE-(t+1) is a
same-thread RMW of the `srow[idx]` UPDATE-(t) wrote; the cross-thread
UPDATE-(t)→PREDICT-(t+1) dependency is published by the post-GATE-(t+1)
barrier). **Disproven by experiment** (`verify_kda_3barrier.sh` +
`ab_kda_barriers.sh`, beverin MI300A): the 3-barrier kernel fails **5 of 6**
delta configs with clean max_rel ≈ 1.4–2.0; the 4-barrier kernel stays 11/11.
The post-GATE barrier is *after* GATE, so it can't stop a race *during* GATE:
GATE-(t+1) on thread `tid` **writes** `srow[idx]` (element `idx%D` of row
`idx/D`) while OUTPUT-(t) on a *different* thread (`tid2 = idx/D`) is still
reading that same row for its dot product. **All four barriers are required.**

1. `omniperf` single-kernel metrics on S=512 D=128 H=128 to localise the
   latency (barrier cost vs PREDICT/OUTPUT thread starvation). NOTE:
   omniperf/omnitrace are **absent** on beverin; `rocprof --stats` works and
   gives per-launch DurationNs but not stall reasons — a counter set
   (`rocprofv3` / `rocprof -i`) is needed for stall attribution.
2. Parallelise the length-`D` dot products (group of threads/row + `__shfl`/LDS
   reduce) so PREDICT/OUTPUT use more of the block — the only intra-block lever
   left now that all four barriers are required.

state traffic** (~96 KB/token/head at D=128, scaling with S and H). At H=128

16 KB at D=128): load once at chunk start, run all four phases on the on-chip
copy, store once at chunk end. Row-parallelism ⇒ each block owns **disjoint**
rows ⇒ no cross-block coordination; gmem state is only the between-chunk
handoff. Math unchanged ⇒ **bit-identical** to `kda_naive_delta_rule_fwd_cpu`

Why slower at low H? At H=1, there's only 1 (b,h) block group × 4 z-blocks = 4 blocks total (D/Db=4). With only 4 blocks on the whole GPU (MI300A has ~228 CUs across 4 GCDs, or ~38 CUs per GCD), the GPU is massively under-occupied. The 4-barrier kernel with Db=32 threads doing the dots means each block uses only 32 of 256 threads — but with 4 blocks that's 128 threads total, all on maybe 4 CUs. The parallel-dot version uses all 256 threads per block = 1024 threads on 4 CUs. 

At low H (few blocks), the extra threads in PAR don't help with parallelism (there are only 4 blocks anyway), but they ADD overhead: the `__shfl_xor` reduction (3 ops × 2 phases × 4 blocks), and crucially the parallel-dot has more threads contending for LDS bandwidth and more barrier participants (256 vs 32 reaching the barrier... wait, no — in the 4-barrier kernel, the GATE/UPDATE loops already use all 256 threads grid-strided; only PREDICT/OUTPUT use 32. Hmm, so why is PAR slower at low H? The dot computation is the same total FMAs (4096/phase), just spread over 8× more threads. At H=1 with 4 blocks, each block's 256 threads do: PREDICT 16 FMAs/thread + 3 shfl, vs 4-barrier's 32 threads × 128 FMAs + 224 idle threads. The PAR version does MORE work per block (the reduction adds ~32*3 = 96 extra adds + 96 shuffles per phase), and with only 4 blocks the GPU can't hide that overhead. Meanwhile the 4-barrier version's 224 idle threads cost nothing (they sit at the barrier). So at low H, PAR's extra reduction work is pure overhead with no parallelism benefit → slower.

At H ≥ 16, there are 16*4 = 64+ blocks → enough to occupy the CUs, and now the question is per-block latency. The PAR version's shorter per-thread critical path (D/r = 16 dependent adds vs D = 128) lets each block finish PREDICT/OUTPUT faster, and with enough blocks to hide latency, the per-block speedup wins → 1.07×.

But 1.07× is modest, and it comes WITH a 12% regression at low H. The low-H regression is the deal-breaker: the K3 production regime (Kimi K3) likely uses H=1 or low H for single-sequence inference, and H=128 for batch. - If the bottleneck were PREDICT/OUTPUT per-block COMPUTE (128 serial dependent adds), parallelising → r-way → 16 dependent adds → per-block PREDICT/OUTPUT time drops ~8× → total kernel time should drop significantly at ALL H (since each token's per-block time drops).

The per-token critical path is: GATE + barrier + PREDICT + barrier + UPDATE + barrier + OUTPUT + barrier. Parallelising PREDICT/OUTPUT reduces the GATE/PREDICT/UPDATE/OUTPUT compute portions, but if those are already small compared to the 4 barrier latencies (each ~hundreds of cycles) and the launch/scheduling overhead, the reduction is invisible. ## Negative result: PREDICT/OUTPUT compute is non-binding (do not parallelise the dots)

Hypothesis: with only `Db=32` of `kTh=256` threads doing the length-`D`
(=128) dots in PREDICT and OUTPUT (12.5% utilisation), each thread runs a
~128-deep dependent add chain — so parallelising each row's dot across
`r = kTh/Db = 8` threads (strided over `e`, `__shfl_xor` butterfly reduce)
should cut the per-block critical path from D to D/r dependent adds and
speed the kernel up at every H.

**Disproven by experiment** (`meta/benchmarks/kda_pardot.hip` +
`meta/scripts/ab_kda_pardot{,_run}.sh`, beverin MI300A, S=512 D=128):

| 1 | 1888 | 2140 | **0.88× (−12%)** |
| 8 | 1897 | 2161 | **0.89× (−11%)** |
| 16 | 2892 | 2707 | 1.07× |
| 32 | 2920 | 2722 | 1.07× |
| 64 | 2935 | 2733 | 1.07× |
| 128 | 3189 | 3055 | 1.04× |

PREDICT/OUTPUT compute were the binding resource, parallelising the
length-D dots would speed up every H, especially low H** (where there is

at H=1 the parallel-dot is 12% *slower* because the per-token critical
path is **not** compute-limited, so the extra `__shfl_xor` reduction is
pure overhead on a path that was already barrier/serial-recurrence bound.

arguments.content:
# kda_delta_rule_fwd — D×D state cached in LDS (2.0×) + per-block limit found

Optimization of the [#70](https://github.com/opentela-ai/vkernels/issues/70) /
#21 KDA primitive, on beverin MI300A (gfx942). Committed `5028461`. Full
write-up + A/B tables in `docs/kda-lds-optimization.md`.

## What was binding (before)
The forward kept the per-`(b,h)` D×D recurrent state in a **global scratch
buffer** and round-tripped it from HBM ~6× per token (GATE rmw, PREDICT read,
UPDATE rmw, OUTPUT read). AI ~0.43 ≪ MI300A ridge ~247 → **memory-bound on the
state traffic** (~96 KB/token/head at D=128, scaling with S and H). At H=128
S=512 D=128 the gmem kernel hits **~3065 GB/s = 58% of the 5300 GB/s HBM roof**.

## The change
Cache each z-block's `Db` state rows in **LDS** (`__shared__ float srow[Db*D]`,
16 KB at D=128): load once at chunk start, run all four phases on the on-chip
copy, store once at chunk end. Row-parallelism ⇒ each block owns **disjoint**
rows ⇒ no cross-block coordination; gmem state is only the between-chunk
handoff. Math unchanged ⇒ **bit-identical** to `kda_naive_delta_rule_fwd_cpu`
(`test_kda_correct` 11/11 PASS, max_rel ≤ 1e-6, verified cleanly on mi300
gfx942 with `g` allocated `[B,H,S,D]` and `rgate` using unsigned modulo).

## A/B (same fixed bench; `ab_kda_lds_vs_gmem.sh` + `ab_kda_scale.sh`)
- Fixed shapes: **2.03×** at S=512 D=128; 1.26×–1.30× at the smaller shapes.
- H sweep (S=512 D=128): **1.64×–2.01×** across H∈{1,8,16,32,64,128}. The win
  is smallest at H≥16 (gmem plateaued at the HBM roof; LDS now latency-bound).

## New binding resource (after) — now localised precisely
The LDS kernel drops to ~13 GB/s actual + ~0.24 TFLOP/s (0.3% of the ~81
TFLOP/s fp32 vector roof): **neither** memory- nor compute-bound. Two negative
experiments localise the real bottleneck as the **serial per-token recurrence
+ four unavoidable per-token barrier latencies**:

1. **4→3 barriers/token is a RACE (do not retry).** Removing the post-OUTPUT
   `__syncthreads` looked redundant (GATE-(t+1) is a same-thread RMW of the
   `srow[idx]` UPDATE-(t) wrote; the cross-thread UPDATE→PREDICT dependency is
   published by the post-GATE barrier). Disproven on MI300A: the 3-barrier
   kernel fails **5 of 6** delta configs with clean max_rel 1.4–2.0; the
   4-barrier kernel stays 11/11. Root cause: GATE-(t+1) on thread `tid`
   **writes** `srow[idx]` (element `idx%D` of row `idx/D`) while OUTPUT-(t) on
   a *different* thread (`tid2 = idx/D`) is still reading that same row for its
   dot product. The post-GATE barrier is *after* GATE, so it can't stop a race
   *during* GATE. **All four barriers are required.**

2. **PREDICT/OUTPUT per-block compute is non-binding (do not parallelise the
   dots).** Hypothesis: only `Db=32` of `kTh=256` threads do the length-D=128
   dots (12.5% util), each a ~128-deep dependent add chain → parallelise each
   row's dot across `r=kTh/Db=8` threads (strided, `__shfl_xor` reduce) to cut
   the per-block critical path 8×. **Disproven on MI300A** (S=512 D=128):
   parallel-dot is **0.88× (−12%) at H≤8** and **1.07× (+7%) at H≥16**, stable
   across runs (summation reorder still passes 11/11, max_rel 1–2e-6 ≪ 2e-2).
   The low-H regression is decisive: if per-block compute were binding,
   parallelising the dots would speed up *every* H, especially low H (no
   occupancy fallback — only `D/Db=4` blocks). It didn't → the per-token
   critical path is barrier/serial-recurrence bound, so the extra `__shfl_xor`
   reduction is pure overhead at low H. The H≥16 win is **occupancy-mediated**
   (more blocks fill the GPU), not a per-block latency breakthrough. Kernel
   committed at `meta/benchmarks/kda_pardot.hip`; repro
   `meta/scripts/ab_kda_pardot{,_run}.sh`.

**Conclusion: the kernel is at its practical per-block latency limit.** No
intra-block optimisation remains — barriers can't be removed (race) and
per-phase compute can't be sped up without regressing the latency-critical
low-H case.

## Remaining lever (not yet taken)
**Token-level pipelining / parallel scan** for inter-chunk parallelism (the
#70 chunked-prefill work): FLA's `C_{c-1}`-decoupled solve lets chunks within a
(b,h) run concurrently once the inter-chunk log-cumsum is known, breaking out
of the one-block-per-(b,h) serial loop. The only scaling lever left; a much
larger architectural change (cooperative kernel splits into intra + inter
passes, as `kda.cpp` already sketches). **Do not revisit** barrier layout or
dot parallelism — both exhausted.

## The #63 "defect" was a test bug, not a kernel defect
The investigation's #70 finding ("kda_delta_rule_fwd incorrect for small
chunked shapes, 5/16 failures") was a **`test_kda_correct` bug**, proven by
fixing it (g allocated `[B,H,S]` but read `[B,H,S,D]` → out-of-bounds device
read once D>1; `rgate` used signed `(int)x % 200000` so `|rnd|` could exceed 1
→ the gate **expanded** the state → 512-step fp divergence amplified to 11%).
With g allocated `[B,H,S,D]` and `rgate` using **unsigned** modulo (g∈(0.05,1.0]
as documented, matching production sigmoid forget gates), **all 6 delta_rule_fwd
configs + 3 layer_norm + 1 gate_cumsum + 1 pack_bitmatrix = 11/11 PASS**,
max_rel ≤ 1e-6. The kernel was correct all along. (Same OOB-g bug fixed in
`bench_kda.hip`, which is why the delta_rule table had never appeared before.)

## Also discovered this session (process)
- beverin's `vkernels-issue63` checkout is at `0ef9966` (original #21), NOT my
  local `5028461` — `git checkout HEAD -- kda.hip` there restores the **GMEM**
  kernel, so any "4-barrier" build via that path is silently the gmem baseline.
  Build the committed kernel from a git-extracted file (or
  `meta/benchmarks/kda_pardot.hip`) instead.
- A direct ssh run (no `srun`) inherits the **default mi200 (gfx90a)** partition
  → a gfx942 binary's kernels do zero work (see [[beverin-cluster-gotchas]]);
  always `srun --partition=mi300` for tests/benches. CMake must configure with
  `-DCMAKE_HIP_ARCHITECTURES=gfx942` (a clean reconfigure that drops this
  compiles libvkernels.a to gfx90a, again → zero work on mi300).
- `omniperf`/`omnitrace` are **absent** on beverin; only `rocprof --stats`
  (per-launch DurationNs, no stall reasons). The two negative A/B experiments
  above localised the bottleneck *without* a profiler — empirical A/B is the
  working profiling method on this cluster.

## Related
- [[issue-63-investigation]]
- [[dsa-topk-gfx942-perf]]
- [[beverin-cluster-gotchas]]

1. **4→3 barriers/token is a RACE (do not retry).** Removing the post-OUTPUT
   `__syncthreads` looked redundant (GATE-(t+1) is a same-thread RMW of the
   `srow[idx]` UPDATE-(t) wrote; the cross-thread UPDATE→PREDICT dependency is
   published by the post-GATE barrier). Disproven on MI300A: the 3-barrier
   kernel fails **5 of 6** delta configs with clean max_rel 1.4–2.0; the
   4-barrier kernel stays 11/11. Root cause: GATE-(t+1) on thread `tid`
   **writes** `srow[idx]` (element `idx%D` of row `idx/D`) while OUTPUT-(t) on
   a *different* thread (`tid2 = idx/D`) is still reading that same row for its
   dot product. The post-GATE barrier is *after* GATE, so it can't stop a race
   *during* GATE. **All four barriers are required.**

2. **PREDICT/OUTPUT per-block compute is non-binding (do not parallelise the
   dots).** Hypothesis: only `Db=32` of `kTh=256` threads do the length-D=128
   dots (12.5% util), each a ~128-deep dependent add chain → parallelise each
   row's dot across `r=kTh/Db=8` threads (strided, `__shfl_xor` reduce) to cut
   the per-block critical path 8×. **Disproven on MI300A** (S=512 D=128):
   parallel-dot is **0.88× (−12%) at H≤8** and **1.07× (+7%) at H≥16**, stable
   across runs (summation reorder still passes 11/11, max_rel 1–2e-6 ≪ 2e-2).
   The low-H regression is decisive: if per-block compute were binding,
   parallelising the dots would speed up *every* H, especially low H (no
   occupancy fallback — only `D/Db=4` blocks). It didn't → the per-token
   critical path is barrier/serial-recurrence bound, so the extra `__shfl_xor`
   reduction is pure overhead at low H. The H≥16 win is **occupancy-mediated**
   (more blocks fill the GPU), not a per-block latency breakthrough. Kernel
   committed at `meta/benchmarks/kda_pardot.hip`; repro
   `meta/scripts/ab_kda_pardot{,_run}.sh`.

**Conclusion: the kernel is at its practical per-block latency limit.** No
intra-block optimisation remains — barriers can't be removed (race) and
per-phase compute can't be sped up without regressing the latency-critical
low-H case.

## Remaining lever (not yet taken)
**Token-level pipelining / parallel scan** for inter-chunk parallelism (the
#70 chunked-prefill work): FLA's `C_{c-1}`-decoupled solve lets chunks within a
(b,h) run concurrently once the inter-chunk log-cumsum is known, breaking out
of the one-block-per-(b,h) serial loop. The only scaling lever left; a much
larger architectural change (cooperative kernel splits into intra + inter
passes, as `kda.cpp` already sketches). **Do not revisit** barrier layout or
dot parallelism — both exhausted.

## The #63 "defect" was a test bug, not a kernel defect
The investigation's #70 finding ("kda_delta_rule_fwd incorrect for small
chunked shapes, 5/16 failures") was a **`test_kda_correct` bug**, proven by
fixing it (g allocated `[B,H,S]` but read `[B,H,S,D]` → out-of-bounds device
read once D>1; `rgate` used signed `(int)x % 200000` so `|rnd|` could exceed 1
→ the gate **expanded** the state → 512-step fp divergence amplified to 11%).
With g allocated `[B,H,S,D]` and `rgate` using **unsigned** modulo (g∈(0.05,1.0]
as documented, matching production sigmoid forget gates), **all 6 delta_rule_fwd
configs + 3 layer_norm + 1 gate_cumsum + 1 pack_bitmatrix = 11/11 PASS**,
max_rel ≤ 1e-6. The kernel was correct all along. (Same OOB-g bug fixed in
`bench_kda.hip`, which is why the delta_rule table had never appeared before.)

- `omniperf`/`omnitrace` are **absent** on beverin; only `rocprof --stats`
  (per-launch DurationNs, no stall reasons). The two negative A/B experiments
  above localised the bottleneck *without* a profiler — empirical A/B is the
  working profiling method on this cluster.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Self-contained A/B build for the parallel-dot experiment. Builds BOTH sides
# from committed kernel variants in meta/benchmarks/ (no beverin-local temps,
# no git-object dependency), into test_kda_4B / kda_bench_4B (oracle-identical,
# Db threads do the length-D dots) and test_kda_PAR / kda_bench_PAR (r=kTh/Db
# threads/row, __shfl_xor reduce, all 256 threads work, per-dot order changed).
# Restore src kda.hip to the committed 4-barrier at the end. Run on the login
# node (compile only); A/B is run separately via srun --partition=mi300.
#
# RESULT (beverin MI300A, gfx942): parallel-dot is 0.88x (12% SLOWER) at
# H<=8 and 1.07x (7% faster) at H>=16, stable across runs. The low-H
# regression is decisive: if per-block PREDICT/OUTPUT compute were the
# binding resource, parallelising the length-D dots (128->16 dependent
# adds) would speed up EVERY H, especially low H (no occupancy fallback).
# It did not — the per-token critical path is bound by the serial
# recurrence + 4 barrier latencies, not thread starvation. The H>=16 win
# is occupancy-mediated (more blocks fill the GPU), not a per-block
# latency breakthrough. Do NOT commit the parallel-dot kernel as a
# replacement (regresses the latency-critical low-H case); the committed
# kda.hip stays. See docs/kda-lds-optimization.md.
set -uo pipefail
SRC=/users/xyao/vkernels-issue63; B=$SRC/build_kda
CLANG=/opt/rocm-6.3.0/lib/llvm/bin/clang++
COMMON="-O3 -std=c++17 --offload-arch=gfx942 -DVKERNELS_HAS_HIP=1 -D__HIP_ROCclr__=1 -I$SRC/src/c -L/usr/lib64/gcc/x86_64-suse-linux/7 $B/src/c/libvkernels.a /opt/rocm-6.3.0/lib/libamdhip64.so.6.3.60300 -lgcc"
KDA=$SRC/src/c/vkernels/kernels/kda.hip
V4=$SRC/meta/benchmarks/kda_4barrier.hip   # committed oracle-identical (Db-thread dots)
VP=$SRC/meta/benchmarks/kda_pardot.hip     # committed r-way parallel-dot variant

build_one () {   # $1 = variant src, $2 = test binary, $3 = bench binary
  cp "$1" "$KDA"; touch "$KDA"
  make -C "$B" vkernels 2>&1 | grep -E "Built target vkernels|error:" | tail -1
  $CLANG $COMMON "$SRC/meta/benchmarks/test_kda_correct.hip" -o "$2" 2>/dev/null && echo "built $(basename "$2")"
  $CLANG $COMMON "$SRC/meta/benchmarks/bench_kda.hip"        -o "$3" 2>/dev/null && echo "built $(basename "$3")"
}

echo "### 1. 4-barrier (oracle-identical, Db-thread dots) ###"
build_one "$V4" "$B/test_kda_4B" "$B/meta/benchmarks/kda_bench_4B"
echo "### 2. parallel-dot (r-way, __shfl_xor reduce) ###"
build_one "$VP" "$B/test_kda_PAR" "$B/meta/benchmarks/kda_bench_PAR"
cp "$V4" "$KDA"   # restore committed 4-barrier kda.hip
echo "### BUILD DONE ###"

# Run INSIDE srun --partition=mi300 (gfx942). Correctness + A/B for the
# parallel-dot experiment. Builds (ab_kda_pardot.sh) must already exist:
#   test_kda_4B  / kda_bench_4B   (oracle-identical, Db-thread dots)
#   test_kda_PAR / kda_bench_PAR  (r-way parallel-dot, all 256 threads)
# Prints correctness (11/11 expected for both; parallel-dot max_rel 1-2e-6
# from the reordered summation, still ≪ the 2e-2 threshold) then the A/B
# table at S=512 D=128 sweeping H. See docs/kda-lds-optimization.md.
set -uo pipefail
B=/users/xyao/vkernels-issue63/build_kda
OLD=$B/meta/benchmarks/kda_bench_4B
NEW=$B/meta/benchmarks/kda_bench_PAR
ulimit -c 0

echo "############ CORRECTNESS (both must be 11/11 PASS) ############"
echo "--- 4-barrier (oracle-identical) ---"; "$B/test_kda_4B"  2>&1 | tail -1
echo "--- parallel-dot (reordered sum) ---"; "$B/test_kda_PAR" 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "############ A/B  S=512 D=128  (H sweep) ############"
printf "%5s %9s %9s %8s\n" H B4_us PAR_us speedup
for H in 1 8 16 32 64 128; do
  o=$("$OLD" "$H" 512 128 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p' | awk '{print $4}')
  n=$("$NEW" "$H" 512 128 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p' | awk '{print $4}')
  sp="-"
  if [ -n "$o" ] && [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" != "0.0" ]; then sp=$(awk -v a="$o" -v b="$n" 'BEGIN{printf "%.2f", a/b}'); fi
  printf "%5d %9s %9s %8s\n" "$H" "$o" "$n" "$sp"
done

The H≥16 win is occupancy-mediated, not a per-block latency breakthrough.

# Device-native mHC projection

`vkernels.torch_ops.mhc_projection` is an optional Torch/Triton inference
operator. The existing NumPy/C++ bindings are unchanged, and importing
`vkernels` or `vkernels.torch_ops` does not import Torch or Triton.

```python
from vkernels.torch_ops import mhc_projection

# Contiguous BF16 GPU tensors: normalized_x [...,16384], weight [24,16384].
# Exactly one or two activation rows; normalization remains the caller's job.
y = mhc_projection(normalized_x, weight)
```

The implementation uses 32 deterministic FP32 split-K partials followed by a
fixed reduction and BF16 output conversion. It has no atomics, modifies neither
input, and does not implement backward. Reduction order differs from BLAS.
`mhc_projection_reference` supplies a Torch FP32-accumulating CPU/GPU oracle.

Call eagerly on every device and token count before graph capture. Triton
autotunes rows/program (1, 2, 4) and warps (4, 8); split-K is currently fixed.
Cold capture raises an error. Warm capture allocates scratch/output from the
graph memory pool. Tuning choices are cached in process, not persisted as a
portable deployment artifact. A new process retunes; do not change hardware or
software underneath a running process. The metadata helper records selected
configurations for benchmark reports.

## Reproduce

Use an environment that already provides compatible Torch and Triton:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src/python python -m pytest tests/python/test_mhc_projection.py -q
PYTHONPATH=src/python python meta/benchmarks/bench_mhc_projection.py --output /tmp/mhc.json
```

On a **beverin `mi300`** node the whole suite (pytest + this benchmark + the
roofline and counter references it relies on) is driven by a single
self-bootstrapping script that also papers over the missing `python3.11-devel`
package — see [`docs/torch-ops-mi300.md`](torch-ops-mi300.md):

```bash
VK63_SECTIONS='2. torch_ops* 3. BENCH mHC*' sbatch meta/scripts/run_issue63_torchops_mi300.sh
```

The benchmark separately measures default BLAS, PyTorch TunableOp-selected
BLAS, and Triton. All tuning/warmup precedes graph capture. Each graph rotates
through 90 independent weights (~68 MiB), with 15 timing samples. This is a
synthetic projection benchmark, not a whole-model throughput measurement.
TunableOp writes a version-validated CSV next to the JSON. The harness does
not install dependencies or enable TunableOp in serving.

## MI300A evidence, 2026-09-08

Beverin job 628593; Torch 2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe, ROCm 7.0.51831-a3e329ad8,
Triton 3.4.0. Captured outputs of every variant were validated before timing.
Median graph GPU latency per projection:

| Activation rows | Default BLAS | Tuned BLAS | Triton |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 146.166 us | 6.647 us | 3.936 us |
| 2 | 146.018 us | 9.288 us | 3.946 us |

The earlier job 628588 measured 146.138 / 11.542 / 4.223 us for one row:
TunableOp solution selection and timings vary between runs, so these are
observations, not universally optimal configurations. Twelve GPU tests
passed, including floe integration, graph replay, cancellation, cold-capture
guard, and non-current-device restoration. One-row synthetic outputs matched
BLAS exactly; two-row maximum relative L2 error was 2.12e-6. These measurements do
not establish general model-quality equivalence. Floe's separate full-model
A/B harness validates logits/NLL/greedy outputs before timing.

# Device-native GLM Q/K/V projection

```python
from vkernels.torch_ops.qkv_projection import qkv_projection

y = qkv_projection(x, q_weight, k_weight, v_weight)
```

Inputs are contiguous BF16 tensors on one GPU: `x [...,4096]` with one or two
activation rows, and three separate `[8192,4096]` weights. Output is contiguous
BF16 `[...,24576]`, ordered Q, K, V. No weight packing, replication, activation
normalization, or intermediate projection outputs are required. The operator
is inference-only and has no backward implementation.

The Triton kernel selects one weight pointer per workgroup, reduces BF16
products in FP32, and rounds each final output to BF16. Reduction order is not
guaranteed to match BLAS. `qkv_projection_reference` provides a CPU/GPU Torch
FP32-accumulating oracle. Torch and Triton imports remain lazy and optional.

Warm up eagerly for every device and row count before graph capture. The
kernel autotunes eight configurations: rows/workgroup 1, 2, 4, 8 and warps 4,
8. Cold capture raises an error. Tuning is cached in process by device and row
count, not persisted as a portable configuration. Retune after stack/hardware
changes. `qkv_projection_tuning_metadata()` records the choices for reports.

## Reproduce

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src/python python -m pytest tests/python/test_qkv_projection.py -q
PYTHONPATH=src/python python meta/benchmarks/bench_qkv_projection.py --output /tmp/qkv.json
```

On a **beverin `mi300`** node the pytest + this benchmark + the TunableOp
preflight (#67) + roofline/counter references are driven by one
self-bootstrapping script that also papers over the missing
`python3.11-devel` package — see [`docs/torch-ops-mi300.md`](torch-ops-mi300.md):

```bash
VK63_SECTIONS='2. torch_ops* 4. BENCH QKV* 5. CHECK frozen*' sbatch meta/scripts/run_issue63_torchops_mi300.sh
```

The benchmark compares three separate BLAS projections plus concatenation,
the same operations using PyTorch TunableOp, and fused Triton. Eight distinct
weight triplets (~1.5 GiB) rotate through each graph. All tuning precedes
capture; captured outputs are validated before 15 GPU timing samples.
Variant order is fixed, so small differences need paired end-to-end follow-up.
The shared graph timing helper lives in `bench_mhc_projection.py`.

## MI300A measurement, 2026-09-08

Beverin job 628602; Torch 2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe, HIP 7.0.51831-a3e329ad8,
Triton 3.4.0. Times include all three projections and baseline concatenation:

| Activation rows | Default BLAS | Tuned BLAS | Fused Triton |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 517.538 us | 75.976 us | 70.106 us |
| 2 | 500.408 us | 76.966 us | 119.076 us |

Triton is fastest here for one-row decode; tuned BLAS wins at two rows. Most
of the one-row gain comes from replacing the default BLAS algorithm, with an
additional ~8% microbenchmark improvement from fusion. The one-row TunableOp
choice was `Gemm_Hipblaslt_208015`; Triton chose one output row/workgroup and
four warps. These are observed choices, not portable optimal settings.

Twelve GPU tests passed, including floe integration, graph replay, read-only
inputs, projection order, cancellation, cold-capture refusal, and restoration
of a non-current device. Maximum synthetic relative L2 error against default
BLAS was 8.72e-5, maximum absolute error 0.0078125. This does not establish
broad real-model quality equivalence.

content.text:
# Device-native mHC projection

`vkernels.torch_ops.mhc_projection` is an optional Torch/Triton inference
operator. The existing NumPy/C++ bindings are unchanged, and importing
`vkernels` or `vkernels.torch_ops` does not import Torch or Triton.

```python
from vkernels.torch_ops import mhc_projection

# Contiguous BF16 GPU tensors: normalized_x [...,16384], weight [24,16384].
# Exactly one or two activation rows; normalization remains the caller's job.
y = mhc_projection(normalized_x, weight)
```

The implementation uses 32 deterministic FP32 split-K partials followed by a
fixed reduction and BF16 output conversion. It has no atomics, modifies neither
input, and does not implement backward. Reduction order differs from BLAS.
`mhc_projection_reference` supplies a Torch FP32-accumulating CPU/GPU oracle.

Call eagerly on every device and token count before graph capture. Triton
autotunes rows/program (1, 2, 4) and warps (4, 8); split-K is currently fixed.
Cold capture raises an error. Warm capture allocates scratch/output from the
graph memory pool. Tuning choices are cached in process, not persisted as a
portable deployment artifact. A new process retunes; do not change hardware or
software underneath a running process. The metadata helper records selected
configurations for benchmark reports.

## Reproduce

Use an environment that already provides compatible Torch and Triton:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src/python python -m pytest tests/python/test_mhc_projection.py -q
PYTHONPATH=src/python python meta/benchmarks/bench_mhc_projection.py --output /tmp/mhc.json
```

On a **beverin `mi300`** node the whole suite (pytest + this benchmark + the
roofline and counter references it relies on) is driven by a single
self-bootstrapping script that also papers over the missing `python3.11-devel`
package — see [`docs/torch-ops-mi300.md`](torch-ops-mi300.md):

```bash
VK63_SECTIONS='2. torch_ops* 3. BENCH mHC*' sbatch meta/scripts/run_issue63_torchops_mi300.sh
```

The benchmark separately measures default BLAS, PyTorch TunableOp-selected
BLAS, and Triton. All tuning/warmup precedes graph capture. Each graph rotates
through 90 independent weights (~68 MiB), with 15 timing samples. This is a
synthetic projection benchmark, not a whole-model throughput measurement.
TunableOp writes a version-validated CSV next to the JSON. The harness does
not install dependencies or enable TunableOp in serving.

## MI300A evidence, 2026-09-08

Beverin job 628593; Torch 2.9.0a0+git7bcbafe, ROCm 7.0.51831-a3e329ad8,
Triton 3.4.0. Captured outputs of every variant were validated before timing.
Median graph GPU latency per projection:

| Activation rows | Default BLAS | Tuned BLAS | Triton |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 146.166 us | 6.647 us | 3.936 us |

BLAS exactly; two-row maximum relative L2 error was 2.12e-6. These measurements do
not establish general model-quality equivalence. Floe's separate full-model

# Device-native GLM Q/K/V projection

```python
from vkernels.torch_ops.qkv_projection import qkv_projection

y = qkv_projection(x, q_weight, k_weight, v_weight)
```

Inputs are contiguous BF16 tensors on one GPU: `x [...,4096]` with one or two
activation rows, and three separate `[8192,4096]` weights. Output is contiguous
BF16 `[...,24576]`, ordered Q, K, V. No weight packing, replication, activation
normalization, or intermediate projection outputs are required. The operator
is inference-only and has no backward implementation.

The Triton kernel selects one weight pointer per workgroup, reduces BF16
products in FP32, and rounds each final output to BF16. Reduction order is not
guaranteed to match BLAS. `qkv_projection_reference` provides a CPU/GPU Torch
FP32-accumulating oracle. Torch and Triton imports remain lazy and optional.

Warm up eagerly for every device and row count before graph capture. The
kernel autotunes eight configurations: rows/workgroup 1, 2, 4, 8 and warps 4,
8. Cold capture raises an error. Tuning is cached in process by device and row
count, not persisted as a portable configuration. Retune after stack/hardware
changes. `qkv_projection_tuning_metadata()` records the choices for reports.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src/python python -m pytest tests/python/test_qkv_projection.py -q
PYTHONPATH=src/python python meta/benchmarks/bench_qkv_projection.py --output /tmp/qkv.json
```

The benchmark compares three separate BLAS projections plus concatenation,
the same operations using PyTorch TunableOp, and fused Triton. Eight distinct
weight triplets (~1.5 GiB) rotate through each graph. All tuning precedes
capture; captured outputs are validated before 15 GPU timing samples.
Variant order is fixed, so small differences need paired end-to-end follow-up.
The shared graph timing helper lives in `bench_mhc_projection.py`.

"""Decode QKV contract checks and optional GPU parity/capture checks."""

import importlib
import subprocess
import sys

import pytest


def test_import_is_lazy():
    subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", "import sys; import vkernels.torch_ops.qkv_projection; "
                    "assert 'torch' not in sys.modules; assert 'triton' not in sys.modules"], check=True)


@pytest.fixture
def torch():
    return pytest.importorskip("torch")


@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", [(4096,), (1, 4096), (1, 2, 4096)])
def test_reference_shape_order(torch, shape):
    from vkernels.torch_ops.qkv_projection import qkv_projection_reference

    x = torch.ones(shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    weights = [torch.full((8192, 4096), scale / 4096, dtype=torch.bfloat16) for scale in (1, 2, 3)]
    actual = qkv_projection_reference(x, *weights)
    assert actual.shape == (*shape[:-1], 24576)
    assert actual.dtype == torch.bfloat16
    assert actual.is_contiguous()
    for expected, part in enumerate(actual.split(8192, dim=-1), 1):
        assert torch.equal(part, torch.full_like(part, expected))


def test_contract(torch):
    from vkernels.torch_ops.qkv_projection import qkv_projection, qkv_projection_reference

    x = torch.ones((1, 4096), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    w = torch.ones((8192, 4096), dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="GPU"):
        qkv_projection(x, w, w, w)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="BF16"):
        qkv_projection_reference(x.float(), w, w, w)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="one or two"):
        qkv_projection_reference(x.expand(3, -1), w, w, w)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="contiguous"):
        qkv_projection_reference(x, w, w.T.contiguous().T, w)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="expected"):
        qkv_projection_reference(x, w, w, w[:4096])
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="share a device"):
        qkv_projection_reference(x, w, w, torch.empty_like(w, device="meta"))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("tokens", [1, 2])
def test_gpu_parity_graph_and_readonly(torch, tokens):
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        pytest.skip("requires GPU")
    pytest.importorskip("triton")
    from vkernels.torch_ops.qkv_projection import qkv_projection, qkv_projection_reference

    torch.manual_seed(173)
    x = torch.randn((1, tokens, 4096), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
    weights = [torch.randn((8192, 4096), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16) / 64 for _ in range(3)]
    before = [tensor.clone() for tensor in (x, *weights)]
    eager = qkv_projection(x, *weights)
    torch.testing.assert_close(eager, qkv_projection_reference(x, *weights), rtol=0.008, atol=0.008)
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        captured = qkv_projection(x, *weights)
    graph.replay()
    torch.testing.assert_close(captured, eager, rtol=0, atol=0)
    for original, tensor in zip(before, (x, *weights)):
        assert torch.equal(original, tensor)

# run_section NAME FUNC -- run a section in a subshell, record rc, never abort.
# A section runs iff no VK63_SECTIONS filter is set, or one of the

declare -A SECTION_RC
_wanted() {  # _wanted NAME -> 0 if NAME should run
  local name="$1" pat
  [ -z "${VK63_SECTIONS:-}" ] && return 0
  for pat in ${VK63_SECTIONS}; do case "${name}" in ${pat}*) return 0;; esac; done
  return 1
}
run_section() {
  local name="$1" func="$2"
  if ! _wanted "${name}"; then
    SECTION_RC["${name}"]="SKIP"; echo "SECTION ${name}: rc=SKIP"; return 0
  fi
  banner "${name}"
  if ( "${func}" ); then
    SECTION_RC["${name}"]=0

## #70 — KDA inter-chunk parallelism: math de-risked on CPU

Fixed real bugs in my own per-key-dim chunked test, in the order the barrier episode taught me to look:

1. **Index bug** in `gate_prod`: read `L[a-1]` (since `k*0 == 0`) instead of `L[(a-1)*D + k]`. With `g==1` all log-cumsums are 0, so the wrong index still read 0 → `exp(0)=1` (that test passed); with random gates it read key-dim 0 for every `k` → exponential divergence.
2. **Call-site mismatches**: the `k3_delta_rule_intra` call was missing `cs` (signature has both `cs` and `c`); the `k3_delta_rule_inter` call passed `u` (vector) instead of `u.data()` and was also missing `cs`.
3. **Pathological test inputs** (g∈(0.01,1], unnormalized v∈[-10,10]) made the recurrence diverge to ~1e25 in *both* paths, turning summation-order round-off into 1e-2 rel error. Switched to the proven stable regime used by the existing standard-rule test (q/k/v∈[-1,1], g∈[0.3,1.0], beta∈[0.3,1.0], absolute 1e-4).

Result: **all 3 tests pass at ≤1e-6 — bit-identical to fp32 round-off** across 7 configs (1–4 chunks, H=2, B=2, D up to 16), full-history (g==1), and single-chunk (random gates). The per-key-dim K3 chunked derivation (gate cumsum → intra triangular solve → inter propagation → output combine, with per-column gate products inside the Gram and post-gate prediction) is **proven correct** — the de-risked CPU foundation for a future HIP chunked kernel. Committed `251d562`. Existing `kda` test still 14/14 (no regression).
